title: Predict: Why Modifier Order Matters
hints: Each modifier returns a *new* view that wraps the previous one.
The outermost type is the **last** modifier you applied.
The two types are different, so the last line prints `false`.
jsBridge: Each modifier **wraps** the view in `ModifiedContent<Inner, Modifier>`, so `padding().background()` and `background().padding()` are different trees. CSS applies properties to one box; SwiftUI builds nested boxes in order.

compass.q: In CSS, `padding` and `background` are properties of one box. Why does order matter in SwiftUI but not in CSS?
Do all modifiers wrap? (Some, like `.font`, flow down the environment.) How do you tell?
When a tap area is too small, which modifier order usually fixes it (`.contentShape`, `.padding` before `.onTapGesture`)?
